headline: THAILAND BLOCKS MYANMAR RARE EARTH CHEMICALS — Export Ban Proposal Goes to Environment Board Dec 2
snippet: Thailand's deputy prime minister confirmed Saturday that the government plans to halt exports of chemicals used in Myanmar's rare earth mining operations in Shan State, citing severe contamination of the Kok River. The formal ban proposal goes to the Pollution Control Committee on November 27 and the National Environment Board on December 2, with China-Thailand-Myanmar talks scheduled for November 24-26. Myanmar's Shan State operations supply a significant share of global critical mineral feedstock and the ban would disrupt a key input supply chain for rare earth processors.

headline: BARKLY RARE EARTHS HITS RECORD 18,086 PPM TREO — 90 of 96 Holes Hit Across 24km NT Corridor
snippet: Barkly Rare Earths (ASX: BAK) reported its highest-grade drill intercept to date at its Northern Territory rare earths project, with hole BAK0240 returning 4,537 ppm TREO over 2.5 metres including a peak of 18,086 ppm TREO over 0.5 metres — 45% above the previous record. The 129-hole wet-season program hit mineralization in 90 of 96 sites across a 24km Northern Territory corridor; a resource update is targeted for the December quarter, building on the current 40Mt at 2,100 ppm TREO resource. Separate metallurgical testing reported 97-98% MREO extraction to acid leach solution.

headline: GOLD SINKS TO $3,514 — 14-Month Low Enters Thanksgiving Week After Worst 5-Day Stretch of 2026
snippet: Spot gold opened Monday at approximately $3,514 per ounce — its lowest level since September 2025 — after completing a 9% weekly decline on Friday, the steepest weekly loss of 2026. Silver trades near $41 per ounce, down approximately 29% from its 2026 peak. With US markets thinning ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, analysts expect reduced liquidity through the remainder of the week, increasing the potential for outsized moves in either direction.

headline: BUY GOLD AT $3,514 OR WAIT? Analysts Split After 14-Month Low — Dollar Strength vs. Central Bank Demand
snippet: Analysts are divided on how to handle gold's correction to 14-month lows. Bulls cite unbroken central bank demand, a widening US federal deficit, and historical patterns showing 30-40% corrections are normal in major gold bull markets. Bears point to 97% CME-implied December Fed rate hike odds and the US dollar near 19-month highs, arguing a retest of the $3,300-$3,400 range remains possible before a sustainable floor forms.

headline: MOUNT HOPE MINING LAUNCHES FIRST DIAMOND DRILL AT MT SOLITARY — 5-Hole Campaign Targets NSW Cobar Basin Gold
snippet: Mount Hope Mining (ASX: MHM) has begun its inaugural diamond drilling program at the Mt Solitary gold project in New South Wales' Cobar Basin — one of Australia's historically productive gold and base metals belts. The 5-hole program marks the transition from surface exploration to deeper systematic testing of a target the company has been building toward, in a district that includes several active ASX-listed junior exploration programs.

headline: CUFE SCOPING STUDY NEAR COMPLETE AT TENNANT CREEK COPPER — First Assays Due December, NT Track Set
snippet: CuFe (ASX: CUF) updated the market that its scoping study at the Tennant Creek copper project in the Northern Territory is near completion, with the first batch of assay results expected in December. Tennant Creek hosts several historical copper-gold mines in a proven mineral field, and the scoping study completion positions CuFe for a development decision timeline in 2027 — coming as copper stabilizes above $14,000/tonne following November's forced-selling correction.

headline: GOLD: 'FINAL SHAKEOUT IS NOW' — FX Empire Sees Key Support at $3,387 Before Longer-Term Trend Resumes
snippet: FX Empire's technical analysis frames gold's current slide to 14-month lows as a 'final shakeout' preceding a resumption of the longer-term uptrend, identifying key near-term support near $3,387. The analysis argues the structural drivers of gold's 2024-2026 bull run — deficit spending, de-dollarization, geopolitical uncertainty — remain intact, and that the current 35% drawdown from January's $5,405 high is consistent with historical major bull market corrections before new highs.

headline: SCOTTIE RESOURCES FEASIBILITY HINGES ON CONVERTING 703K OZ INFERRED — Will 25.5 g/t Blueberry Results Upgrade?
snippet: Discovery Alert's analysis of Scottie Resources (TSX-V: SCOT) argues that its H1 2027 feasibility study depends entirely on converting the project's 703,000-ounce entirely Inferred resource to Indicated and Measured categories. The 2026 program — 61,578 metres across 227 holes including recent results of 25.5 g/t gold over 14 metres and 120 g/t gold over 1.5 metres at Blueberry — builds the geological data needed for that conversion, but how many ounces survive the classification upgrade will determine whether the feasibility study shows bankable economics.
